findings.summary: The cached-decode self-consistency tolerance (0.5 for BF16 and F16) is gpt-oss's batched-row tolerance and was never measured on decode steps. Transformers' own BF16 cached decode, teacher-forced on the same tokens, departs from its stateless pass by more than 0.5 on four of the five Llama-family checkpoints (up to 1.75 on Qwen2-7B) and on gemma-3-4b-it (up to 1.5625), while its F32 decode stays within 2.6e-4. Burn's decode path is as consistent in F32 (1.26e-4 on Qwen3-4B, 1.80e-4 on SmolLM3-3B, 2.44e-4 on gemma-3-4b-it) and on Metal/F16 equals the stateless pass exactly on all five Llama-family checkpoints. The Flex/BF16 cached greedy gates of Qwen3-4B (0.5625, the only step above 0.5), SmolLM3-3B (0.515625; the full dump reaches 0.75) and gemma-3-4b-it (0.625 at 53f167b, 0.75 at c2936fe) fail on this tolerance alone: their cached prefills, decisive greedy steps and batched rows pass. The decoded-longest-prompt checks these failures never reached would pass by the dumps' approximation (Qwen3-4B mean 0.04932 against 0.05204; SmolLM3-3B 0.09218 against 0.09465).

findings.summary: feed_forward::apply_activation evaluates SiLU with Burn's activation::silu, x * sigmoid(x), which in BF16 and F16 rounds sigmoid(x) before the product; PyTorch's F.silu evaluates in F32 and rounds once (the function's own documentation at c2936fe says so). At position 0, where attention is trivial, Burn Flex/BF16 SmolLM-135M and the official MPS BF16 model with its activation replaced by x * torch.sigmoid(x) show the same per-block residual distance from F32 through all 30 blocks and the final norm and the same position-0 logit maxima (1.166528, 1.435591); the diagnosing session reports the dumps bitwise equal there (the committed logs carry the distances, not the raw dumps). The rounded SiLU alone accounts for SmolLM-135M's prompt-1 maximum failure. A scratch patch evaluating SiLU in F32 (harness/patched-silu/src/feed_forward.rs, never committed) brings prompt 1 to 1.1741, but prompt 2 (2.0306 against 1.9828; mean 0.13211 against 0.08464) and SmolLM3-3B's prompt-1 mean (0.09868) still fail, so the patch turns no gate green. It would change the half-precision numerics of every SiLU family (Llama, Qwen3.5/3.8, Qwen3-MoE, DeepSeek-V2, Muse, custom and MoE specs) and add F32 intermediates on Metal/F16; if adopted, every half-precision gate of those families must run again.

findings.summary: At 53f167b the Gemma Flex/BF16 prompt-logits gate failed (prompt 1: 0.7699 against 0.7106). The root cause was the crate's tanh GELU: Burn's composed gelu_approximate rounds each of its operations and both constants to BF16, while Gemma's gelu_pytorch_tanh evaluates in F32 and rounds once. Swapping that rounded graph into the official model reproduces Burn at position 0 (99.9% of block-0 residual entries identical, against 69.8% for the unmodified model) and pushes the official model itself out of the rule on prompt 2. c2936fe evaluates F16/BF16 tanh GELU in F32 and rounds once; F32 and F64 are unchanged (all F32 lines identical at both heads). At c2936fe the gate passes with prompt maxima 0.346, 0.514 and 0.582 (bounds 0.460, 0.711, 0.897), and on Metal/F16 Burn's block-0 residual matches the official F16 model in 91% of entries instead of 73%.
